citation.title: Acute changes in antioxidants and oxidative stress to vigorous arm exercise: an intervention trial in persons with spinal cord injury and healthy controls

reported.what: Able-bodied controls (n = 6): high-intensity bouts of arm cranking set as 85-95% of peak heart rate; VO2, RER and lactate were not measured during them, and the load is in watts of arm cranking, which is not the cycle work rate the model converts

location.where: Methods and Results, high intensity interval exercise
location.quote: 3 bouts of 4 min at an intensity of 85–95% of the peak heart rate

reported.what: Able-bodied controls: peak heart rate, peak VO2 and blood lactate at maximal effort of a ramp arm-cranking test to exhaustion (Table 2, control columns, pre-test and maximal effort); the ramp's duration is not printed, the fed state is not described (only no food in the hour before), and the lactate sampling time of the pre-test is not printed
Able-bodied controls: peak oxygen uptake of the pre-test

detail: The only bouts are arm cranking at a percentage of peak heart rate with no oxygen uptake measured, and ramps to exhaustion whose duration is not printed, so no bout intensity and length can be written; the paper prints no resting heart rate, pressure, lactate or other value of the controls, and the participants' table holds only anthropometry.
